title: Address-search reliability under GeoSearch failure + ZoLa-first human-readable property links

acceptance_scenarios.description: A transient GeoSearch 503 followed by a successful response recovers within the bounded retry policy; suggestions appear; the user's typed text is never cleared.
Repeated 503s produce a specific source-unavailable outcome (not a generic 'unavailable'), stop retrying at the bound, and present the manual/Geoclient fallback prefilled with the typed text.
A valid reply arriving after the deadline is a distinct timeout outcome; an explicit full-address search action is offered; no indefinite deadline raise.

A complete pasted address submitted without a highlighted suggestion goes through the explicit /search action and always lands on candidate confirmation - the first approximate suggestion is never auto-accepted as the lot.
Genuine no-match and incomplete-address are distinct outcomes with distinct wording; neither is presented as a service failure.
HTTP 429 is classified as rate-limit, distinct from 503 source failure, with bounded backoff.
A malformed or non-PAD-validated payload yields a validation-failure outcome; no partial or invented suggestion is rendered.
Queens hyphenated house numbers and at least one address per borough resolve through the repaired flow in deterministic fixture tests.
Editing the query cancels superseded in-flight work; a stale response never overwrites newer suggestions.

With a valid, conflict-free lot identity the primary source link is the ZoLa lot page (constant prefix + validated BBL); the current PLUTO JSON record is demoted to a clearly secondary raw-record link; the dataset landing link remains; invalid, absent, or conflicting identity renders honest absence; every existing M5-T030 wrong-lot/wrong-source/conflict test stays green.

A dated live smoke check (GeoSearch autocomplete + /search + one ZoLa lot URL) is recorded in the producer report as live evidence, separate from deterministic tests; deterministic tests do not require live internet success.

risks: GeoSearch autocomplete and /search share one upstream service - recovery design must not present endpoint switching as an independent fallback (handoff section 6)
Full suite + browser journeys run at the integration seam per D-064-R007; producer runs the focused commands only
